definitions.explanation: The warhead portion of a nuclear weapon — the part containing the fissile or fusion material that delivers the explosive yield. Typically used in news, policy, and security contexts when discussing missiles that carry nuclear payloads.

examples.japanese: {核弾頭|かくだんとう}を{搭載|とうさい}したミサイル。
examples.english: A missile loaded with a nuclear warhead.

examples.japanese: その{国|くに}は{数|すう}{百|ひゃく}{発|ぱつ}の{核弾頭|かくだんとう}を{保有|ほゆう}している。
examples.english: That country possesses several hundred nuclear warheads.

examples.japanese: {新条約|しんじょうやく}のもと、{両国|りょうこく}は{実戦配備|じっせんはいび}された{核弾頭|かくだんとう}の{数|かず}を{削減|さくげん}することに{合意|ごうい}した。
examples.english: Under the new treaty, the two countries agreed to reduce the number of deployed nuclear warheads.

notes:
Composed of {核|かく} (nuclear, from {核兵器|かくへいき} "nuclear weapon") and {弾頭|だんとう} (warhead, literally "tip/head of a projectile"). The word refers specifically to the warhead — the part of the missile that actually detonates — rather than the delivery vehicle (missile, bomber, submarine) itself.

USAGE:
- Most often counted with the counter {発|はつ} (rounds): {十|じゅう}{発|ぱつ}の{核弾頭|かくだんとう} (ten nuclear warheads).
- Appears constantly in newspaper articles about arms control, proliferation, and security policy.
- A single missile can carry multiple warheads — referred to as {多弾頭|ただんとう} (multiple warheads) or MIRVs in English.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {核弾頭|かくだんとう}を{搭載|とうさい}する: to load/mount a nuclear warhead
- {核弾頭|かくだんとう}を{保有|ほゆう}する: to possess nuclear warheads
- {核弾頭|かくだんとう}を{削減|さくげん}する: to reduce nuclear warheads
- {核弾頭|かくだんとう}の{配備|はいび}: deployment of nuclear warheads
- {実戦配備|じっせんはいび}の{核弾頭|かくだんとう}: operationally deployed nuclear warheads

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {核兵器|かくへいき}: nuclear weapon — the broader term covering warheads and delivery systems
- {弾頭|だんとう}: warhead — the generic term, not necessarily nuclear
- ミサイル: missile — the delivery vehicle
- {核|かく}: nuclear — used as a prefix in many compounds ({核実験|かくじっけん} "nuclear test," {核保有国|かくほゆうこく} "nuclear-weapon state")
- {原爆|げんばく}: atomic bomb — a historical/specific term often referring to the bombs dropped on Hiroshima and Nagasaki
